transcript.question: Is Cameron Coscia's aggressive, nine-move waiver approach with The Stinky Faggots smart roster-building, or is it papering over a starting lineup that's living off boom weeks from Bijan Robinson and Rico Dowdle?

hotSeat.why: Nina Sharpe is favorite on them (+72), Curtis Vaughn is neutral on them (+9)

sides.mel-diaper: Nine waiver moves and only $24 of the $100 budget spent tells you Cameron Coscia is hoarding FAAB instead of fixing real roster holes.
sides.reggie-banks: The Stinky Faggots are 5-3 with 1094.2 points for, fourth in the standings — the results say Cameron Coscia's process is working, full stop.

turns.speaker: curtis-vaughn
turns.text: Good evening. The Stinky Faggots are 5 and 3, tied for the league's most active roster with nine waiver pickups, and Cameron Coscia just spent this week's budget on Will Reichard and the 49ers defense for a combined zero dollars. So here's the question: is Cameron Coscia building this roster the right way, or is he just riding a bench that keeps bailing him out? Mel, you're up.

turns.speaker: mel-diaper
turns.text: NINE PICKUPS AND TWENTY-FOUR DOLLARS. TWENTY-FOUR! Cameron Coscia is sitting on $76 of $100 in Week 8 like it's a goddamn savings bond. Meanwhile Week 7 came in at 105.4 and lost. That's not roster-building, that's window shopping. My number: The Stinky Faggots finish outside the top two seeds — no better than third — because you cannot hoard $76 and call it a plan.

claim.text: The Stinky Faggots finish no better than 3rd — outside the top two seeds — because Cameron Coscia is hoarding $76 of FAAB instead of fixing the lineup

turns.speaker: reggie-banks
turns.text: Seventy-six dollars in the bank and FIVE AND THREE on the field! 1094.2 points, fourth in the league — that's not window shopping, that's a bad man who doesn't need to overpay.
